The other are Power Source tokens that will features in various card effects. These need to be placed around the board before a Setup card is pulled. Other named spaces are the Best Friend's House, the Community Pool, Fanghorn Forest, the Library, the School, and the Town Fair.

== Gameplay ==
There are two unique gameplay mechanics for Falconwood: Missions and River Crossings.

=== River Crossings ===
Certain spaces have blue lines connecting them, making them river crossings. They do not count as adjacent spaces, and are not normally traversable unless dictated by a special event.

=== Missions ===
When beginning a game in Falconwood, you must choose a Mission to complete. Completing the Mission is mandatory to win the game, and you cannot turn over the Killer's final health marker until the Mission is completed.

Upon completing the Mission, you will gain a Friend. Friends are considered Special Victims but they will not panic and will enter the Killer's space with you.

== Layout ==

The Nexus also doubles as a Search space, with the other two Search spaces being the House of Mutilation and the Sepulchre of Blood.

== Gameplay ==
Gameplay for the Hellscape centers around the shifting Hellscape tiles, four tiles around the outer perimeter of the board. The tiles are double-sided, and during each Upkeep phase special dice are rolled to determine that either a tile will flip, or two tiles will swap their locations on the board. Other effects can cause the Hellscape tiles to change, and the player is able to move Hellscape tiles themselves: either through certain Items, or the unique Action card '''[[Hellshift]]'''.

''"The town of L'Armes was abandoned centuries ago. War ravaged the area countless times, to the point that locals believed the land was cursed. No one remembers how the town got its name...some claim it was because weapons had been stockpiled there during the various wars; while others claim it was due to all the weeping over the souls that have been lost. Maybe it was both, or maybe it was neither...no record exists of the origin. Ursuline nuns had the abbey built in the hopes of converting the many non-believers in the area, but the horrible events in the abbey just further reinforced their belief that the area was indeed cursed and that there was no god interested in helping them."''

''- Amelie Rosier, local historian''

'''L'Armes Abbey''' is the featured Location in the Series 4 Feature Film [[A Demon in the Shadows]].

== Layout ==
L'Armes Abbey has 18 spaces. There are three exits, in the northeast, southeast and southwest of the board. The search spaces are the Sacristy, the Museum, and the Kitchen. Six spaces are designated "Field Spaces" with a wheat icon. One space in the northeast of the board is designated the "Altar of the Old Gods".

== Gameplay ==
L'Armes Abbey includes the Malice mechanic and the Blessed and Cursed Dice.

=== Malice ===
A game starts with four Malice tokens on the board, one in the Killer's space and one in each of three adjacent spaces (if only two spaces are adjacent, the player chooses a space adjacent to one of those spaces).

Various cards increase Malice by placing a new token in the Active Killer's space or the closest possible space chosen by the player. If all 14 Malice tokens are on the board and a 15th would need to be placed, the game ends in a loss.

If the player is in a space with a Malice token, they must replace one regular (red) die with a black Cursed die.

A Malice token can be removed with the Benediction Action card.

=== Blessed Die ===
The Blessed die is translucent gray. It gives better results when included in rolls, with two stars on the 6 face, one star on the 2 face, and only one blank face (1).

=== Cursed Die ===
The Cursed die is black. It gives worse results when included in rolls, with a Partial Success symbol replacing the star on the 5 face and a Lose 1 Health symbol on the 1 face.

'''Sunnydaze Mall''' is the featured Location for the Series 3 Feature Film [[The Killer From Tomorrow]].

== Layout ==
Sunnydaze Mall has 22 spaces. There are 2 exits, to the Southeast and Northwest (Service Entrance). Five of the spaces are Railing spaces, leading to the Food Court. The search spaces are Military Surplus 'R Us, Stan's Sporting Goods, and the Zap Shack. The other three Stores are Boards 'N Bones, Joystick Heroes, and Smokin' Subject, with the remaining named spaces being the Atrium and Security.

== Gameplay ==
The gameplay for Sunnydaze Mall has three main mechanics: the Savior, Railings, and Stores

=== [[Savior|The Savior]] ===
The Savior is a young teenager who is being targeted by the Killer. The Killer will target them in place of you when resolving Terror Cards, and if they die the game is lost immediately. The Savior has a [[Trust]] feature, determining how they will react to you. You can build trust with the dedicated [[Trust|Build Trust]] Action card, until you are able to either have them survive longer than the Killer, or escape.

=== Railings ===
There are 5 Railing spaces on the upper floor of the Mall. The Final Girl or Savior can jump from them to the Food Court below, with the risk of taking damage if they do. Enemies will not jump over the railing, but if anyone takes damage on a Railing space, they will be sent to the Food Court and lose additional Health.

=== Stores ===
When anyone takes damage in a Store space, they will be sent through one of the walls into another space. This destroys the wall, causing them to be adjacent spaces, and also causes damage to the recipient.

== Lore ==
{| class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed fandom-table"
|+'''Hans' Lore'''
|'''The campers sat around the fire, pretending to listen to another one of Edwin's "famous" spooky stories. But all of them were pissing the counselor off. "Listen up you little pissants!" That got their attention. "Clearly the stories haven't been scary enough, so we'll cut the kiddie crap!" He paused for effect, which more or less worked. "Have you ever heard of Hans?"'''
'''"You mean the guy in the piggie mask? Big deal." One smart ass threw back in his face.'''

'''"It's called a German Shame Mask, dipshit. Now listen up." For once, they did.'''

Hans made everyone in the small town of Happy Trails uncomfortable. The boy never spoke, which was part of it. He would tag along with his parents and older siblings whenever they came to town to hawk their wares, staying in the back of the butcher stall, looking down on everyone. That was also a source of the unease: his freakish height. Although he was the youngest child in the Metzger clan, a family of butchers who had immigrated from Germany, he towered over all of them, even Helmut, the family's imposing patriarch. But his height and lack of speech weren't the real reasons why the town avoided him and children ran in fear. It was the wooden pig mask he wore. "That's just my naughty little liebchen, always too hungry for his own good," Ada, his mother, would say when asked about it. The townsfolk came to understand that Hans was being punished for his gluttony, forced to display the shame for all to see. His appetite must have been ravenous; he was never seen without his mask, although wet munching sounds could be heard from beneath it.

Hans was tolerated because the meat the Metzgers sold out of their stall was better than anything else in town. Putting up with their giant, mask-wearing freak was a small price to pay for pork chops and rib eyes of this quality. Over time, things changed. Fewer of the children came to the market ("They are tending the arm while we are gone,"), Ada began to waste away ("A recent illness, that is all"). Hans' presence remained unchanged, with the exception that his wooden mask had been replaced by a brutal looking iron one. The residents of Happy Trails said nothing publicly. Privately, they began to enjoying their steak dinners less and less.

One month, the Metzgers simply didn't appear at the market. No Helmut, no Ada, no Hans, and no prime rib. The town decided to send a small search party to the farm to check on the family. They found it deserted. The house was empty. No animals grazed in the pasture. An eerie quiet lay over the entire property, as if even the birds and insects had left. The last place they looked was the barn, an imposing red structure behind the main homestead that the Metzgers had used as their slaughter house. They opened the doors and went inside.

Afterwards, the search party refused to talk about what they had seen. Instead, they burned the barn and the rest of the farm to the ground and walked back to Happy Trails with the look of soldiers returning from war. "The Metzgers are gone," is all they would say. The other butchers in town went out of business; the appetite for meat evaporated over night.

Animals began disappearing first. A goat here, a cow there, every so often a beloved family dog. The first child to go missing shocked Happy Trails, which had always been a safe community, but it was only after the fourth had disappeared that people began to leave. Thomas Hoffstetter said he saw an enormous dark shape drag Maria Woodson into the dark. Others said they heard crunching sounds coming from the woods at night. Most believed them and fled. Some remained out of stubbornness. That year was a census year, but when the census takers arrived at Happy Trails, they found it utterly empty. Many of the doors were open, with rotting meals on the table, as if the families living there had simply disappeared mid-bite. Eventually, the town was razed and forgotten. Happy Trails: Population 0.

"Years later, this camp was built on top of where the town once was. Over there?" Edwin pointed off into the dark. "That's were the Metzger's farmstead used to be. If you listen carefully, you can still hear Hans wandering through the trees, munching on something wet and chewy beneath his iron mask." As all of the campers turned to look, they heard a wet crunching sound in the trees. Right on cue they screamed, with some even hightailing it in the opposite direction. Edwin began to lauch. "You little punks, we PLANNED that. Zeke was hiding in the woods waiting to make his Hans sounds until I finished the story-"

The last thing Edwin heard was a sickening crunch as his skull collapsed in a geyser of bone and scarlet. The immense figure behind him in an iron pig mask hoisted the giant hammer, now slick with blood, and surveyed the remaining campers, some fleeing into the woods and others frozen in fear. In the flickering firelight, it looked as if the mask was smiling. Hans couldn't help but admire the lovely buffet that had been delivered to his home, like pigs to the slaughter.
|}

Dr Fright is the featured Killer in the Series 1 Feature Film [[Frightmare on Maple Lane|A Frightmare on Maple Lane]]. 

Dr Fright starts at 9 Health and 4 Horror.

== Appearance ==
Dr Fright appears as a middle aged man with decaying skin, eyes opaque like a corpse, and lanky mid-length gray hair. He wears an archetypal therapist's sweater vest and undershirt with a red bow tie and slacks. His face and clothes are cratered with holes in his flesh and fabric, and he's often seen with a toothy, sinister grin.

== Gameplay ==
'''Special Setup''': Shuffle the Boiler Room cards and place them facedown. Then place the Awake/Asleep card on top of the deck with the Awake side faceup. This is the Boiler Room deck.

Dr Fright's primary game mechanic are the states of Awake and Asleep. When you are Awake the game proceeds as normal, but when you are Asleep you enter the Boiler Room, the dream realm that Dr. Fright stalks.  Your current state is determined by which side of the Awake/Asleep card, and you begin the game as Awake.

Whenever the game says you go to or fall Asleep, take the Awake/Asleep card and, without flipping it, slide it under the bottom of the Boiler Room deck. Then, flip the deck over. If you have done this correctly, the Asleep side of the card should be faceup on top of the deck. You are now Asleep and inside the Boiler Room.

Some Terror cards will cause you to fall Asleep, but if you want to trigger this voluntarily you can resolve a Short Rest or Long Rest card during the Action phase. Regardless of the result, apply the normal effects and fall Asleep.

'''When you are Awake:''' You can move, search, and save Victims as normal. Dr Fright is NOT able to attack you and you are NOT able to attack him. When Dr Fright resolves a "Target Final Girl or Victim" Killer action, treat it like a "Target Victim" action instead unless an effect allows him to attack you while Awake. When Dr Fright resolves a "Target Final Girl" Killer action, he will still move toward you but CANNOT attack you. (If he ends his turn in a space with a Victim, however, he WILL attack them.)

'''When you are Asleep:''' You can move around, attack Dr Fright, or even search for items. However, Dr Fright can now attack you, and will resolve Killer actions as normal. Victims will NOT follow you, nor are you able to save them. You also MUST resolve one Boiler Room card at the end of the Killer phase.

To defeat Dr Fright you must fight him in the Boiler Room, which is the only state in which you can damage him. To exit the Boiler Room, you must finish out the Boiler Room deck. In order to resolve a Boiler Room card, you must slide the deck of cards up, down, left, or right, such that half (or sometimes a quarter) of the card beneath is revealed. You cannot slide it in a direction where no part of the card would be revealed. If the card reveals an image of Dr Fright, he attacks you with the Killer action "Target Final Girl > Attack." You may defend as normal.

You will successfully leave the Boiler Room by resolving all cards in the deck, and then you may flip the deck to awake. Immediately shuffle the Boiler Room cards facedown and place the Awake/Asleep card on top as Awake.

== Lore ==
Dr Fright was once known as Dr Franklin Wright, a renowned "dream therapist" gifted with psychic abilities that allowed him to treat his patients by manipulating their dreams. This power came with a quick price, as he rapidly begin experimenting on his patients by introducing dark and frightening content to their dreams. His theory was that, by having patients confront their worst fears in dreams, they would learn to overcome their problems in the real world. It worked for just enough patients that he was able to get away with it as a revolutionary new cure.

Everything changed when a new patient, Lisa Smalley, had the opposite reaction to his experimental modality and jumped from the roof of her high school. Her parents blamed Dr Wright, earning him his nickname of Dr Fright. The resulting scandal ruined him and his practice fell apart. 

Instead, he began touting his methods online, and so developed a cult following in spite of the mockery that trailed him. He learned that he could enter his subjects' dreams from anywhere, and also that the trauma experienced in dreams left real-life wounds on the victims. When a skeptic named Scally offered to try Wright's therapy in order to disprove it for an audience, they were instead treated to his wrists mysteriously opening up on a live stream. He died from blood loss before the paramedics could reach him. 

Meanwhile, the Smalleys had been tracking Wright for a long time, determined to bring him to justice, whatever the means. Employing a private eye, they traced him to a makeshift office in the boiler room of an abandoned factory in town. The Smalleys kidnapped him to their farm, and decided to give him a slow and terrible death at the end of a pitchfork. As Wright died, he managed to escape into the dreamworld, and ever since it has been the realm from which his desiccated spirit enacts its revenge.

Geppetto is the featured Killer for the Series 1 feature film [[Carnage at the Carnival]]. 

Geppetto starts with 8 Health and the Horror level at 4.

== Appearance ==
Geppetto is a tall, thin man with a pale face and a wide, Joker-ish grin. He wears a top hat and a circus ringmaster's suit, with pinstriped pants. He's often shown wielding a puppeteer's control bar from which he manipulates his living marionettes. 

== Gameplay ==
Before the Finale is revealed, Geppetto must resolve the following Killer action:

Spawn 1 Puppet > Target Victim > Movement

==== Special Setup ====

* Place the Puppets card next to the Killer board
* Place all 3 Puppet tokens on the Ready space on the card

Geppetto's main Killer mechanic is the deployment of his Puppets, who can attack Victims or the Final Girl. Puppets are considered [[Minions]], but the following rules apply to Puppets specifically. 

There are a maximum of 3 total Puppets that can be on the board or the Puppet card at any time. Whenever a Puppet is killed, place it on the Exhausted space on the Puppet card.

Each Killer phase up until the Finale is revealed, the first step in the Minion Action line on the back of the Finale card is to spawn a Puppet. When spawning a Puppet, take a token from the "Ready" space of the Puppets card and place it in Geppetto's space. If there are no tokens in the Ready space, no Puppet is spawned. Whether one is spawned or not, move all the Puppet tokens in the Exhausted space into the Ready space.

Some of Geppetto's Terror cards will specify whether an Action line only applies to Puppets, but many do not. When resolving a Killer action on any Terror card that does NOT specify whether it only applies to the Puppets, each Puppet on the board will resolve the full action one at a time. If there are multiple Puppets, you may choose which order they resolve the action in. After each Puppet has gone, resolve the same action for Geppetto.

Puppets have 1 Health and their attack value is 1 Damage. Their Movement value is the same as Geppetto's and will change accordingly when his Bloodlust increases. These stats are located on the Puppets card as a reminder. Puppets must end their movement within 2 Spaces of Geppetto. They may move farther than 2 spaces from him as long as they END their movement within 2 spaces from him. This can sometimes happen when a Puppet's target is within 2 spaces of Geppetto, but taking the most direct route to reach that target will momentarily place them 3 or more spaces away from him. 

If a special effect from a Terror card or other game effect results in a Puppet being more than 2 spaces away from Geppetto, the next time that Puppet must choose a target, it will instead target Geppetto, attempting to end its movement as soon as it is exactly within 2 spaces of him. If it runs out of movement it may be forced to stop farther than 2 spaces from Geppetto, in which case it will repeat this process the next time it must choose a target.

When a Puppet must stop moving, either because further movement would cause it to end more than 2 spaces from Geppetto OR it was returning to Geppetto and made it exactly 2 spaces from him, any additional movement it may have had is lost.

== Lore ==
While Geppetto's exact origins are unclear, he is a serial killer who cobbled together his first puppets from the remains of his victims, aided by the occult as indicated by the texts of ancient rituals found around [[Creech Manor|his former home]] in one of the scenarios. He later founded a circus where he could cull visitors to produce more "children," whom he sees as more perfect than the flawed, unruly patrons, even the ones he chooses as worthy targets for conversion. At some point, he had a daughter, [[Barbara Romero|Barbara]], with an unknown mother. (Whether or not Geppetto's last name is also Romero is unknown.) His puppets help him control much of the circus, but he also hires out partial staff who seem somewhat aware of his nefarious behavior.

* [[A Life of Their Own|'''A Life of Their Own''']] - [[Selena Villanueva|Selena]] finds herself dragged along by her boyfriend to a ghost hunt at the former home of a serial killer who made puppets out of his victims. When the marionettes come out of the walls to attack, she turns to the occult items she's found in the house to save them.
* [[Honor Thy Father|'''Honor Thy Father''']] - [[Barbara Romero|Barbara]] fights to escape Geppetto's grasp in the [[Sacred Groves]], where the puppet master has come to collect his daughter with the intent of making her "more perfect."

{| class="mw-collapsible fandom-table"
|+Poltergeist's Lore
|'''Creech Manor is a home that is over 100 years old. It has the kind of character and charm that people love. It is the kind of home where every step, every new room, can call to one's imagination a story from the past. The wise reader would stop reading now and keep whatever happy, sunshine beaming through the majestic windows, pictures they have in their head... for what follows will stick like a shadowy leech onto your soul forever.'''
'''The happy imagined stories the average person would envision are a far cry from the real and actual horrible events that have taken place in the manor over the years. The below accounts are just a few of the many atrocities that have occurred in the home.'''

1912

The original owner named Robert Creech, a wealthy commodities trader and statesman, was found hanging in the attic by his much younger wife, Helen. She inherited the wealth and was able to do a great deal of good with it, but eventually, the money ran out. She went up to the attic one night and ingested a concoction of champagne and a large amount of rat poison, unaware of how slow and painful the process of her death would be. During the investigation, the neighbours that lived half a mile away, said they heard a horrific wailing, coming from the direction of the manor, that lasted most of the night.

1957

Tim Grace was a boy of thirteen when he came back home from the circus with a brand new clown doll. He was on top of the world! At night, he'd keep the clown sitting up on the chair across the room. He felt safe with it watching over him. One night, a fierce lightning storm came through the area. Tim was staring at the clown and each time the lightning flashed in the darkness, the clown's expression seemed to change. When it's eyes turned red, he was sure of it and threw his blanket over the clown and the chair. The next day when he woke up, the clown and the blanket were both gone. Tim was relieved but confused. For the next eleven days Tim pleaded with his parents to move, claiming "the clown doll attacks me every night!" But when they observed him at night, it seemed to just be night terrors and bad dreams. They saw no doll. They would finally be convinced to move by the suffocation death of their son just a few days later. He was found with a blanket wrapped so tightly around his head, you could see the shape of his screaming face in the blanket.

1981

Lucy loved staring out of the window at the old oak. She wondered if it was older than the manor itself. It was obviously the oldest tree in the neighborhood. She smiled as the wind bristled its leaves. Such a beautiful tree. As the days went by she spent more and more time at the window. When her husband came home from work one day and found her in the exact same spot as when he left that morning, he became concerned. He tried to get her help and Lucy resented him from that moment forward. How dare he take her away from the tree. When they returned that night, they shared no words and went to bed under an awkward silence. Lucy woke up in the early hours of the night and went to the window. The tree, who had been speaking to her for some time now, offered to protect her. It reached out its largest branch towards the window and opened what can only be described as a hand-shaped branch in front of her. She opened the 3rd floor window and climbed onto the sill. She hesitated, but then looked up at the tree itself. Smiling, she stepped forward and plummeted to her death.
|}

{| class="mw-collapsible fandom-table"
|+'''Evomorph's Lore'''
|'''When the Konrad first became infested after raiding an abandoned and decrepit space freighter, the crew had no idea that a hatchling Evomorph had returned with them.'''
The hatchling invaded the body of one of the crew by crawling into one of their orifices. Hatchlings incubate inside the host's body until they reach a size where the host is no longer sufficient in size or provided nutrients. At that point, it bursts forth from the host creating its own orifice and killing the host.

Younglings hunt and feed on whatever living beings they can find. They are incredibly quick and deadly. While their exoskeleton is tough, they can be damaged and even killed with human-designed weapons. They are also very susceptible to fire. Once a Youngling has fed on enough victims, it will evolve into its full-grown Adult form.

Adult Evomorphs can survive for several years on no food. They hunt purely for sport as they instinctually learn while being a Youngling, even though they are often only in that stage for a matter or hours. An Adult Evomorph is essentially a killing machine and will even attack other Evomorphs for sole superiority.

When there is nothing to kill, because the Evomorph is alone on a planet or ship, it will then begin to nest out of boredom. It does not produce eggs in large numbers making only one Hatchling each year. A Hatchling can only survive without a host for about a year itself, so it is extremely rare to have more than one or at most two hatchlings in an area at a time.

If an Evomorph is unable to find a new source of food, it will perform a process called morpholosion where it can use its dying body to preserve the Hatchling almost indefinitely. This process is the reason why Evomorphs have continued to exist despite the fact that they kill any and every living thing around them.

Eventually, the cycle continues when the hatchling is introduced to an area with a living organism. The hatchling has acute biological sensors and when it senses such a being, will "hatch" from the morpholosion cocoon to seek out the being as its host.

Evomorphs have eradicated full ship crews and even full planets, though they are often killed before such extreme destruction in cases where they find themselves among a highly populated, well-armed place or in a place with beings more dangerous than the Evomorph, which is rare but possible.

One thing is for sure, the crew of the Konrad is hardly a group that is likely to survive an encounter with an Evomorph.

'''The Organism''' is the featured Killer in the Series 2 Feature Film, '[[Panic at Station 2891]]'. The Fast, Strong, and Tough Organisms begin with 5, 6, and 7 Health respectively, and all games begin at 5 Horror.

== Appearance ==
All of the Organisms resemble mutated pale-skinned humanoids covered in yellow boils. The Fast Organism has an additional set of arms, and walks on all of its limbs, with tentacles sprouting from its body, and multiple eyes running along its back. The Strong Organism is a hulking figure, with two heads fused together and bony armor coating its arms and hands, turning them into large spikes. The Tough Organism is bloated, with its mouth extending down its torso, a tentacle spewing mouth growing from one shoulder, and a multi-jointed pincer growing from the other.

== Gameplay ==
There are two main aspects to the Organism's gameplay - Exposed Victims, and the Mutated Organisms.

=== Exposed Victims ===
When setting up the games, three Victims will be replaced at random with Exposed Victim meeples. These three Victims (represented by a Red, Black, and Gray meeple) have the potential to be Organisms. You can use a Test Kit (obtained from Search spaces, with one per space) or the Lab space (if playing at Station 2891) to draw a random Test Result card. Similarly, any effect that would kill the Victim results in a card being drawn.

If the card reads SAFE, then that card is removed from play and the Exposed Victim is replaced with a regular yellow meeple. If the draw was prompted by the Victim's death, the bloodlust goes up as normal.

If the card reads ASSIMILATED, then that Victim becomes one of the Organisms, revealed by flipping one of the facedown cards on the Killer board. They are set up with Health and a Final Health token, and all Bloodlust effects are activated at once to match the current Bloodlust level. The ASSIMILATED card is shuffled back into the Test Result deck.

=== Mutated Organisms ===
Mutated Organisms are considered Killers and not Minions. If multiple Organisms are in play, they complete their Killer actions one at a time, beginning with the leftmost Organism on the Killer board. Upon reaching the Finale, each Organism has an additional set of Killer Actions that they perform in addition to their usual Killer Actions at the beginning of the Killer phase.

'''The Intruders''' are the featured Killer in the Series 2 Feature Film '[[A Knock at the Door]]'.

The Intruders start at 3 Horror and 6 Health per Killer.

== Appearance ==
The Intruders are a trio of killers.

Trish is the leader, and is a Caucasian woman wearing a white tank top and green boiler suit that is tied around her waist. On her head is a mask made with an animal skull, and decorated with sticks, leaves and fur. She wields an axe.

Baghead is a towering man in a white button-up shirt and blue dungarees. On his head is a sack, with eye holes cut into them in a misshapen way that suggests his head underneath is deformed. He wields a large blade.

Zeke is the smallest of the three, and is a Caucasian man wearing a white t-shirt, brown overshirt, and denim jeans. On his face is a mask painted with a grinning face. He wields a blade.

== Gameplay ==
The unique gameplay of the Intruders relies on their use as a trio of Killers. All three Killers begin in the same starting space, but only one is considered the Active Killer. The Active Killer behaves as a solo Killer would in regards to Killer Actions and Terror Cards, while the other two Killers remain inactive.

=== Changing the Active Killer ===
There are three ways the Active Killer shifts:

# Once a Killer is attacked or damaged, they instantly become the Active Killer.
# Certain cards have the effect of changing the Active Killer.
# When the Active Killer is killed, the top-most Killer becomes the new Active one.

Krampus.texto:
Krampus is the featured Killer in the Special Feature film [[The North Pole Nightmare]]. 

Krampus starts the game with 10 Health points and 4 Horror.

== Appearance ==
Krampus is goat-like bipedal creature with mane of shaggy gray hair and pointed elfin ears. A pair of massive horns crown his head and his mouth seems to perpetually hang open to reveal a long reptilian tongue. 

According to the Lore, before his banishment he and Santa resembled one another as men with "brown and black curly hair and beards."

== Gameplay ==
Before the Finale is revealed, Krampus must begin the Killer phase by resolving the following:

Target Final Girl or Victim > Attack > Target Final Girl or Victim > Movement > Leave a Present

==== Special Setup ====

* Shuffle 4 Krampus Presents (goat icon) cards to form a deck. Shuffle the 4 Santa Presents (Santa hat icon) cards to form a separate deck. Place both Presents decks near the play area.
* Shuffle all the Present tokens face down and keep them nearby for use during the game.

Krampus's main mechanic is to leave Presents in his path (represented by Present tokens) as he moves about the location. The Presents can either be positive or negative based on whatever token was randomly placed there. When a Present icon appears as an effect on a card, roll a die and place a random, unrevealed present token in or adjacent to Krampus's space according to the number rolled and the Panic numbers on Krampus's space. If there is already a Present token in that space, do not place a new one. (No Present is placed.)

Presents can be opened by you or Victims. To open a Present, flip the present token over to reveal the effect. Some Presents have small tricks or rewards, such as added or decreased Horror, Time, etc. Other Presents have either the Krampus or Santa icon, and when found you must draw a card from the corresponding Present deck and apply the effects as indicated. 

* '''Final Girl Opening a Present:'''  While in a space with a Present token during the Action phase, you MAY choose to reveal the Present. You may even open a Present while moving through a space by immediately revealing it and applying the effect before continuing your movement.
* '''A Victim Opening a Present:''' Whenever a Victim is in the same space as a Present, no matter how they or the Present got there (even if they followed you into the space), the Victim must open it. Immediately reveal the Present. If it is a Santa present, discard a Santa card with no effect on yourself, as the Victim keeps the present for themselves. If a Victim reveals a Krampus Present, draw a Krampus Presents card and resolve it as indicated. In all other cases apply the Present's effects on YOU, even if you're not in the same space.

== Lore ==
A long time ago, Krampus and Santa were companions on the yearly Christmas visit to children across the world; it was Santa's duty to bring gifts to the good children, while Krampus brought punishment to the naughty ones--often violently. As the number of naughty children began to dwindle, Santa wondered if Krampus was needed at all, to say nothing of the horror Santa felt at his brother's methods. When Santa, for the final time, told Krampus that it should be his last Christmas on the sleigh, his brother was exiled from the North Pole--cursed to transform into a hideous creature if he tried to return. Krampus nonetheless plotted to overthrow Santa and resume his cruel work. For many years, and of his own accord, he tormented not only naughty children but everyone with the misfortune of encountering him. One Christmas night, the "lord of darkness" visited Krampus and offered him the power he sought, at the cost of trading his human shape for the form of a horned monster. It was then that he set his sights on the North Pole for revenge.

== Scenarios ==
Krampus features in a deluxe scenario pack released for Christmas 2024. This pack contained 12 scenarios, visiting every Location produced for Series 1 and 2:

* '''[[Twas the Week After Christmas]]''' - Krampus attacks [[Santa's Village]], as he has done every fifty years since his banishment. [[Mrs. Claus]] works to kill him.
* '''[[Twas the Week After Christmas (Flashback)]]''' - Following his defeat, Krampus wanders the Arctic until he comes across [[Station 2891]].
* '''Horns Aplenty''' - Seeking souls to restore his power, Krampus comes across [[Wingard Cottage]], right before a band of guests (including [[Ava Tyler|Ava]]) are due to arrive.
* '''[[I'm Your Fairy God-Krampus]]''' - Krampus is summoned to the [[Storybook Woods]] by a witch. The witch asks Krampus to kill her great-niece [[Chantelle "Red" Gilliam|Red]].
* '''[[Your Presents is Requested]]''' - The witch transports Krampus to the [[USS Konrad]] as it is about to reach Earth. He decides to kill the crew on board, including [[Ellen]].
* '''[[Come See the Amazing Krampus!]]''' - Krampus hides out in the [[Carnival of Blood]]. Once he realises it is booby-trapped, he gets to killing the guests, including [[Eihi Asami|Asami]].
* '''[[Christmas Comes to Creech! (Flashback)]]''' - In a flashback, [["It's Santa!"|Santa]] took Krampus with him to [[Creech Manor]], to make distractions while he left presents.
* '''[[Getting Inside... of Santa's Head (Part 1)]]''' - Trying to understand Santa's mind, Krampus travels to [[Maple Lane]] to leave his twisted presents in every house.
* '''[[Getting Inside... of Santa's Head (Part 2)]]''' - To understand the North Pole's defenses, Krampus "defends" the [[Sacred Groves]] from the tourists defiling it.
* '''[[A Quick Side Quest]]''' - Krampus pays a visit to [[Wolfe Asylum]] to kill an annoyance of his who was recently committed there - Buddy the Elf.
* '''[[A Nest of Naughty]]''' - On his way to the North Pole, Krampus senses the huge concentration of naughty children in [[Camp Happy Trails]] and takes a detour.
* '''[[Twas the Night Before Krampmas]]''' - On Christmas Eve, Krampus returns to Santa's Village, ready to end Santa once and for all!

Razorface is the featured Killer of the Series 3 feature film [[Hell to Pay]]. 

Razorface starts with 9 Health and the Horror level at 5.

== Appearance ==
Razorface is a demonic humanoid with yellowish pale skin, no hair, and his lips and nose removed as if sliced off. His body is scored with ritualistic cuts, most visible on his scalp and face. He wears what appear to be an array of leather straps across his chest and leather braces on his forearm. Ringed piercings attached to thin chains bind the skin around his torso to the straps on the underside of his upper arms. Around his waist he wears a black leather or cloth wrap that vaguely resembles a butcher's apron with sharp devices of torture dangling from it. In the illustration for his Killer board, he clutches in one hand a human heart pierced with needles.

== Gameplay ==
Play against Razorface begins with 3 Affliction cards assigned to the Final Girl. In order to kill Razorface for good, the player must Purge each Affliction by meeting its Purge Requirement. During the Action phase, if the Purge Requirement has been met, you may choose to Purge the Affliction by resolving the Purge Effect at the bottom half of the card. If you choose not to purge the Affliction when the requirement is met, then the Purge Requirement needs to be met again later in order to Purge the Affliction. Once an Affliction has been Purged, remove it from the game. Some game mechanics throughout play will give the Final Girl more than the initial three Affliction cards at setup.

'''Impossible Afflictions:'''  Sometimes conditions required to Purge an Affliction are no longer possible (such as an Affliction Requirement relating to Victims when there are no more Victims on the board). When this occurs, remove the Affliction from the game and draw a new one from the Affliction deck. You automatically lose the game if you need to draw and Affliction card and none remain.

Razorface's Final Health token may ''only'' be revealed if there are ''no'' Afflictions in play. As such, any damage done to Razorface while Afflictions ''are'' in play that would otherwise reveal the Killer's Final Health token is ignored.

The Slayer was once known as Dr. Henry Slayer, a scientist in one of [[Falconwood]]'s government labs. In summer of 1979, his colleague Dr. Matthew Ross records that he and Henry were able to open a small rift in space, from which several "plant-like" tendrils emerged and touched Henry's hand. From then on, Henry began having strange dreams and visions that very much interested Dr. Owen Martin, the lab's shady new Director of Operations. Weeks later, they manage to open a bigger rift from which many tendrils wrap themselves around Henry, and he is even more changed for it, being suddenly able to read people's emotions and move things with telekinesis. Henry's new powers allow him to see Dr. Owen's intention of exposing a group of children to the interdimensional tendrils, and he ultimately destroys the lab, supposedly perishing in a wormhole he opened up by overloading the equipment. Many years later, Dr. Ross notes the sudden disappearances around town and reports of a humanoid figure abducting them. He speculates that the figure might be Dr. Slayer, returned from the other dimension to claim his victims.

The scenario ''From Death Comes a New Life'' confirms Ross's speculation by depicting Slayer shortly after he's thrown into the wormhole during the destruction of the lab, finding himself mentally in the Hellscape as his humanity is erased and his body transformed into the Slayer. He later begins his rampage of revenge against Falconwood, particularly Owen Martin and the children (Janelle among them) who managed to survive the lab.

Hunter.texto:
The H.U.N.T.E.R. (Human-like aUtomaton for Necessary Threat Elimination and Removal) is the featured Killer for the Series 3 feature film [[The Killer From Tomorrow|The Killer from Tomorrow]]. There are technically two H.U.N.T.E.R.S.: the Mark V and the Mark X, with the Mark X replacing the Mark V as the main killer near the end of the game using a countdown mechanic. 

The H.U.N.T.E.R. starts with 15 Health and 5 Horror, but the Health value only applies to Mark X. 

== Appearance ==
'''Mark V''': The Mark V is effectively a human-shaped android, with an uncannily tall and boxy, wide-shouldered frame dressed in a leather jacket, red hoodie (the hood up to cover its head), and black pants--presumably to help disguise its inhuman identity. Its outer skin resembles that of a human, which hides the silver machinery underneath depicted in one of the Dark Power cards, while electric blue eyes shine out from under the red hood. In its main illustration for the game, it carries with it a shotgun in one hand. 

'''Mark X''': The improved model of H.U.N.T.E.R., the Mark X better resembles a human, taking the form of a much nimbler-looking woman with long black hair and purple eyes, dressed in a more formal style of dark shirt and pants with a white collared undershirt. 

== Gameplay ==
Before the Finale is revealed, the H.U.N.T.E.R. begins the Killer phase by resolving the following:

* Target Final Girl -> Movement -> Attack

'''Part 1: The Mark V'''

In the initial phase of the game, the Final Girl battles the Mark V, whose damage is counted via the Cybernetic Part tokens placed on top of the two Mark X Countdown tokens on the Finale card. (Five tokens in total.) The Hunter Mark X Terror card should be set aside and shuffled in with the bottom three cards of the Terror deck. The Mark V meeple goes on the board first, with the silver Mark X meeple out of play until the conditions to trigger that phase of the game are met. A Mark V Ally card and 4 action cubes should also be added alongside the setup for future use when the Killer switches to Mark X.

For both H.U.N.T.E.R.s, Bloodlust only increases if it does damage to the Final Girl or to an ally, or if the H.U.N.T.E.R. is damaged itself. This represents the machine's cybernetic brain learning from each encounter. Bloodlust can only be increased once in this way per phase, so a phase in which both the H.U.N.T.E.R. and Final Girl take damage (via cards like [[Retaliate]]) only increases its Bloodlust by one point rather than two.

The final health token and health markers on the Killer board are for Mark X only. Mark V instead receives damage by destroying its Cybernetic parts, which require two points of damage each to remove.  Damage can accumulate from multiple attacks, but cannot carry over to subsequent phases; that is, for a part to be destroyed the two or more points of damage have to occur in the same phase. So a one point of damage done during the Action phase by a Weak Attack does not destroy a Part if the Final Girl Retaliates for one point of damage in the Killer phase, etc. Multiple Cybernetic Parts can be removed with one or more multiple attacks in the same phase.

When a Cybernetic Part is destroyed, remove the token from the Finale card and roll a die to place the Part in or adjacent to the Mark's V space according to the number rolled and the corresponding Panic numbers on its space. 

When all the Cybernetic Part tokens are removed, the Mark V is defeated and shuts down. Leave its meeple on the board, then take its Dark Power card, revealing it if it's still facedown, and slide it under the Mark V Ally card so that its special ability is showing at the bottom. If the Mark V was defeated during the Action phase, you may continue your turn. Otherwise, the phase immediately ends. For the rest of the game, Mark V is no longer considered a Killer or an Enemy.

'''Part 2: The Mark X'''

When all Cybernetic Parts have been removed and only countdown tokens remain on the Finale card, ignore the Killer action on the Finale card and do not draw a Terror card. Instead, remove a Countdown token at the beginning of the Killer phase and increase the Bloodlust by 1. When the second Countdown token is removed (as well as when resolving the Mark X Terror card), draw a new Setup card and place the silver Killer meeple for the Mark X at the starting space indicated for that card. The Mark X is now the active killer.

The player can retrieve Cybernetic Parts with your Backpack to repair the Mark V and convert it into an Ally. To pick up a Part token, spend one Time point during the Action phase while in the token's space. For multiple tokens in a space, each requires you to spend one Time point. Keep the tokens facedown when adding them to your Backpack. Cybernetic Parts may be picked up before Mark V is defeated. 

Once you have one or more Cybernetic Parts in your Backpack and the Mark V has been defeated, you may begin re-installing them on the Mark V to repair it. While in a space with the Mark V, spend one Time point to flip over one Cybernetic Part token in your Backpack and place that many Health markers on the Mark V Ally card. The first time a Cybernetic Part token is flipped, also place the Mark V Ally card in your play area along with the four Action Cubes. Mark V is now considered an Ally. Further repairs can occur in the same manner by spending Time for each token and adding the effects to the Mark V, which increases the Mark V's Health. Once an Ally, if the Mark V loses all its Health it is permanently destroyed and removed from be board. Further repairs cannot be made once its Health is at zero. (See the [[Allies]] rules for further info about playing with the Mark V Ally.)

The Volk'ar appears as a purple humanoid alien. She has knife-shaped horns at her cheeks and the top of her head; six yellow eyes along the sides of her face; two forward-facing nostrils; and fangs extending above and below her jawline. She wears armor and a red loincloth, with a one-horned ape-like skull as a pauldron, and large blades attached to her forearms. She has elongated feet and seems to mostly rest on her toes, rendering her stance slightly satyr-like.

After revealing the '''Setup''' card, do not place the '''Killer''' meeple onto the board. Instead, place an '''Origin''' marker onto the space where the '''Killer''' would begin and place the second '''Origin''' marker onto the back of the single face down '''Movement''' card.

Whenever you are instructed to Unleash Killer Wrath, check the current level on the Killer Wrath card and apply any effects listed there. The effects can be anything from increasing Horror, performing a Killer action, or increasing Inkanyamba's health.

Some card effects will let you reduce Killer Wrath, but the main way to reduce Wrath is to purchase and play the [[Atonement]] Action cards, which may be played only during the Action phase.

'''L'Armes Abbey''' is the featured Location in the Series 4 Feature Film [[A Demon in the Shadows]].

== Layout ==
L'Armes Abbey has 18 spaces. There are three exits, in the northeast, southeast and southwest of the board. The search spaces are the Sacristy, the Museum, and the Kitchen. Six spaces are designated "Field Spaces" with a wheat icon. One space in the northeast of the board is designated the "Altar of the Old Gods".

== Gameplay ==
L'Armes Abbey includes the Malice mechanic and the Blessed and Cursed Dice.

=== Malice ===
A game starts with four Malice tokens on the board, one in the Killer's space and one in each of three adjacent spaces (if only two spaces are adjacent, the player chooses a space adjacent to one of those spaces).

Various cards increase Malice by placing a new token in the Active Killer's space or the closest possible space chosen by the player. If all 14 Malice tokens are on the board and a 15th would need to be placed, the game ends in a loss.

If the player is in a space with a Malice token, they must replace one regular (red) die with a black Cursed die.

A Malice token can be removed with the Benediction Action card.

=== Blessed Die ===
The Blessed die is translucent gray. It gives better results when included in rolls, with two stars on the 6 face, one star on the 2 face, and only one blank face (1).

=== Cursed Die ===
The Cursed die is black. It gives worse results when included in rolls, with a Partial Success symbol replacing the star on the 5 face and a Lose 1 Health symbol on the 1 face.

mec:Savior.texto:
The Savior is an otherwise unnamed [[Allies|Ally]] from the Series 3 feature film [[The Killer From Tomorrow|The Killer from Tomorrow]], and is specifically featured in the rule set of the [[Sunnydaze Mall]] location. He is a teenager upon whom the future of the human race depends and whom the Final Girl must protect in order to succeed. 

== Description ==
The Savior is depicted as a White teenager with messy blond hair and a permanent scowl. He wears a blue hoodie with white sleeves and a pair of jeans.

According the scenario [[10 Years Earlier...The First Meeting]], the Savior is possibly [[Kat]]'s child, whom she later comes back to rescue from the [[The H.U.N.T.E.R.|H.U.N.T.E.R.]]  in [[Saving the Brat]]. Depending on the Event cards pulled, he may have a [[The Savior's Girl|girlfriend]] who is also the protagonist of the Character Pack [[Elisabeth's Rebellion]].

== Rules ==
(The Savior uses game mechanics related to [[Allies]].) 

The Savior comes with his own Ally card and starts the game with 4 Health. If the savior dies, the game is instantly lost regardless of the Final Girl's remaining Health. He does not have a Final Health token. The Savior is the Killer's primary target. Whenever the Killer would target the Final Girl they instead target the Savior.  (These rules are in addition to the default Ally rules.)

In spite of his future heroic identity, the teen Savior of the present is kind of a jerk and doesn't trust the Final Girl trying to save him and, therefore, the fate of humanity as well. The player must build trust with him using the [[Build Trust]] action cards to make the marker on his accompanying [[Trust]] card rise high enough to convert him into an Ally. As trust levels are gained, new abilities and positive outcomes are unlocked for both his Ally actions and the [[Savior Card]] results. If the Savior's Trust level is at its highest ("I Believe You!") and he is in an Exit space, he may exit the board during the Action phase. If he does so, you immediately receive all unclaimed Victim rewards on your Final Girl card and your Ultimate Ability is unlocked. If your card is already flipped, receive the Additional Victims Saved reward three times. Once the Savior exits, you'll once again become the Enemy's target when they are targeting you, and the game will end as normal with either the Killer or the Final Girl's health reaching zero.

During the Panic phase, the Savior will panic the same way Victims do.

== Ally Card Abilities ==
All lower-level trust abilities are available at higher levels as well.

Trust Level 1 (Eat Me!)

* Reduce damage from attack by 1
* Recover Health

Trust Level 2 (I Guess You're Ok)

* Move 1 Space
* Move 1 Space

Trust Level 3 (I Believe You!)

* Lower Horror level by 1

Trust is a game mechanic for the [[Savior]] as part of the [[Sunnydaze Mall]] location in the Series 3 feature film, [[The Killer From Tomorrow|The Killer from Tomorrow]]. 

Trust can be raised via Build Trust action cards and is tracked by a marker on the corresponding Trust Level card. The level of Trust impacts the Savior's [[Allies|ally]] status and abilities, as well as the outcomes of [[Savior cards]].

== Trust Levels ==

* Go to Hell! (Level 1):  Cannot exit the board. Cannot use any Ally actions.
* Eat Me! (Level 2): Cannot exit the board. Can only use the bottom 2 Ally actions.
* I Guess You're OK (Level 3): Cannot exit the board. Can only use the bottom 4 Ally actions.
* I Believe You! (Level 4): Can exit the board. Can use all Ally actions.
